A useful rule is Second derivative test: f''>0 up, f''<0 down. You can learn Concavity by trying one small example instead of long theory."

      - article:
        - heading "UNDERSTAND" [level=3]
        - paragraph: The sign of the second derivative determines concavity.
      - article:
        - heading "▣ Rule (Concavity Test)" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Let f be twice differentiable on an open interval I.
        - paragraph: • If f″(x)>0 on I, f is concave up.
        - paragraph: • If f″(x)<0 on I, f is concave down.
        - paragraph: • If f″ changes sign at c, f has an inflection point.
      - article:
        - heading "Worked Example (this function)" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Given f(x) = −8x⁴ + 4x³
        - paragraph: f′(x)=−32x³+12x²
        - paragraph: f″(x)=−96x²+24x
        - paragraph: "Inflection candidates: 0, 0.25"
        - paragraph: Test each interval using the sign of f″.
      - article:
        - heading "⚠ Common Misconception" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Thinking “above the x-axis” or “below the x-axis” decides concavity.
        - paragraph: "✕ Wrong: Graph position doesn't determine concavity."
        - paragraph: "✓ Right: Concavity depends on the sign of f″ (slope behavior), not the height of f."
